title: Catch a thought
intro: When an urge or a low mood hits, an automatic thought is usually riding along with it. Slowing down to examine it takes away its automatic power.

steps.prompt: What was happening? Describe the situation.
steps.hint: Where were you, what were you doing?
The exact thought, in your own words.

steps.prompt: How strong was the feeling or urge?
What's a more balanced way to see this?
steps.hint: Not forced positivity — just fairer and truer.

title: Spot the distortion
intro: Urges love a distorted thought. Naming the distortion loosens its grip.

steps.prompt: Which pattern does it fit best?
Rewrite the thought without the distortion.

title: Trigger analysis (A-B-C)
intro: Antecedent, Behaviour, Consequence. Mapping the chain shows you where you can step in next time.

steps.prompt: Antecedent — what came before? (time, place, mood, situation)
Consequence — how did you feel afterwards?
Where in that chain could you do something different?
steps.hint: The earlier the link, the easier to break.

title: Delay & decide
intro: You don't have to say no forever — just not right now. Delay creates the space for the urge to pass.

steps.prompt: How strong is the urge right now?
How long will you delay before deciding?
What will you do during the delay?
steps.hint: Pick something that changes your state or place.

steps.prompt: Come back after: how strong is the urge now?
